user.title: First probe
user.description: Pair a cheap soil probe with a water deficit computed by a scientific model. The probe is read as an index from 0 to 100; the deficit is the reference the probe will be calibrated against. You can add more probes now, and any time later from the integration options.

data_description.name: How this probe will appear: it names its device and its entities.
data_description.moisture_entity: The raw sensor of the cheap probe, exactly as it is published today.
data_description.deficit_entity: A soil water deficit in millimetres or inches, produced by a water balance model.
data_description.ambient_temperature_entity: Used to refuse samples while the ground is frozen, and as a fallback when the probe reports no temperature of its own.
data_description.irrigation_entity: Improves the timing of the drainage window. Without it, irrigation is inferred from the deficit collapsing.
data_description.probe_temperature_entity: Leave empty unless discovery picks the wrong one. The probe temperature is the sentinel that notices a flat battery.
data_description.sheltered_from_rain: Tick for a probe under a roof, in a greenhouse or on a covered terrace. The rain gauge is then never applied to it: the sky over the lawn says nothing about soil the rain cannot reach.

soil.title: Soil reservoir
soil.description: The deficit counts missing millimetres; the probe answers about water content. These values are the reservoir that converts one into the other. If the deficit comes from NeverDry, use the same soil you configured there. Not sure which one it is? The two minute ribbon test is described in the documentation: {soil_doc}

data_description.root_depth: How deep the roots that matter reach. It sets how many millimetres of deficit correspond to one point of water content.
data_description.field_capacity: Water content the soil holds after drainage, in cubic metres per cubic metre.
data_description.wilting_point: Water content below which plants cannot extract water.
data_description.saturation: Porosity. Leave empty to assume a margin above field capacity.

confirm.title: Companions found on the probe

add_another.title: Another probe?
add_another.description:
Configured so far: {count} ({names}).

Tick the box to add another probe now. You can also add probes later from the integration options.

rain.title: Rain gauge (optional)
rain.description:
If the site has a rain gauge, the calibration can count a shower as an irrigation: it opens a drainage window, closes the dry-down cycle and starts the next one. Rain also becomes evidence about placement, because it wets the whole surface while a dripper only wets a bulb around itself.

Leave the entity empty if there is no gauge. Rain then reaches the calibration the way it always has, through the water deficit collapsing, which sees downpours and misses showers.

data.rain_quiet_minutes: Silence that ends a rain event

data_description.rain_entity: A sensor publishing millimetres or inches of precipitation. Leave empty to configure no gauge.
data_description.rain_sensor_type: Per event for a tipping bucket, where the value is the depth of the last tip. Running total for a daily, rolling or lifetime counter, where only the increase counts.
data_description.rain_quiet_minutes: A valve says when it closes; rain does not. After this long without a new millimetre the event is over, and the drainage window starts from the last drop rather than from now.

error.moisture_out_of_range: The probe must publish an index between 0 and 100.
error.deficit_not_numeric: That entity does not publish a number.

add_probe_soil.description: The reservoir this probe sits in. If the deficit comes from NeverDry, use the same soil you configured there for that zone. Not sure which one it is? The two minute ribbon test is described in the documentation: {soil_doc}

edit_probe_detail.title: Edit {probe}
edit_probe_detail.description: Changing the raw probe sensor or the deficit source invalidates the calibration: the collected samples describe a different instrument.

edit_probe_soil.title: Soil of {probe}
edit_probe_soil.description: Correcting the soil re-derives the collected history against the new reservoir and drops the current calibration, which then has to be earned again on the same data. The samples themselves are measurements and survive. Not sure which one it is? The two minute ribbon test is described in the documentation: {soil_doc}

confirm_removal.title: Remove {probe}?
confirm_removal.description: This deletes the device of {probe}, its entities and every cycle it has collected. Those cycles took weeks of calendar time to gather and cannot be recovered.

data.confirm_removal: Yes, remove this probe and its history

sampling.title: Sampling rules
sampling.description: Which observations are allowed to become samples, for every probe of this installation. Defaults suit a garden bed on a daily irrigation cycle.

data.min_soil_temperature_c: Refuse samples below this soil temperature

data_description.drainage_minutes: Time the wetting front needs to redistribute. Readings inside this window describe water in transit, not what the root zone keeps.
data_description.probe_timeout_s: How long the probe temperature may be silent before the probe is treated as dead, typically a flat battery.
data_description.min_soil_temperature_c: Frozen water does not behave like liquid water in a capacitive reading.

gates.title: Quality gates and write-back
gates.description: How much evidence a calibration must have before it is published, for every probe of this installation. Lowering these publishes sooner and trusts less.

data.allow_device_writeback: Allow writing an offset into the probe

data_description.min_cycles: A cycle is one irrigation followed by a measurable dry-down. Five cycles is the default: a single wetting event is the most common way to get a confident and wrong calibration.
data_description.allow_device_writeback: Off by default. When enabled, the apply_device_offset service may change a probe's own calibration, which drops every sample collected so far.

calibrate_now.name: Calibrate now
calibrate_now.description: Refit the calibration immediately from the cycles collected so far and report whether it passed its quality gates. Does not lower the gates: a calibration that lacks evidence stays unpublished.

probe.name: Probe
probe.description: Name of the probe. Leave empty to refit every configured probe.

reset_calibration.name: Reset calibration
reset_calibration.description: Throw away every sample, cycle and fit of one probe and start collecting from scratch. Use after moving the probe to another spot.

probe.name: Probe
probe.description: Name of the probe to reset. Required: a reset throws away weeks of collected cycles, so it never acts on every probe at once.

mark_field_capacity.name: Mark field capacity
mark_field_capacity.description: Declare that the soil around one probe is at field capacity right now, recording its current reading as a wet anchor. Call it after watering thoroughly and waiting for the soil to drain.

probe.name: Probe
probe.description: Name of the probe to anchor.

apply_device_offset.name: Apply offset to the probe
apply_device_offset.description: Write a calibration offset into the probe's own calibration entity. Requires the write-back option to be enabled. Every collected sample of that probe is dropped afterwards, because it no longer reports what those samples describe.

probe.name: Probe
probe.description: Name of the probe to write to.

offset.name: Offset
offset.description: Offset to write. Leave empty to use the value the calibration suggests, which is refused when the fitted gain is too far from the device scale for an offset to help.

export_samples.name: Export samples
export_samples.description: Return every sample, cycle and fit behind the current calibrations, for inspection or for a bug report.

probe.name: Probe
probe.description: Name of the probe. Leave empty to export every configured probe.

irrigation_threshold_too_low.title: Irrigation waters too often to calibrate {probe}
irrigation_threshold_too_low.description:
The zone behind {deficit_entity} irrigates at {configured} mm of depletion, but a calibration cycle must cover at least {required} mm, which is thirty percent of the {reservoir} mm this soil can hold.

With this regime the soil never dries enough between two irrigations: no cycle will ever count as evidence and {probe} will stay uncalibrated indefinitely.

Raise the irrigation threshold of that zone to at least {required} mm, which is also ordinary practice for the plants it waters, or lower the required cycle span in the integration options and accept a weaker calibration.

placement_no_response.title: {probe} is not reading the water it is supposed to read
placement_no_response.description:
Over {cycles_considered} irrigation cycles the soil went from field capacity to nearly dry, and the index published by {moisture_entity} travelled {median_raw_span} points in the meantime.

A probe inside the wetted soil cannot stay still while the reservoir empties. Worth checking in this order: the probe sits outside the volume the irrigation actually wets, it sits above or below the root zone the deficit describes, or it is in a gravel pocket or a void where there is no soil water to sense.

Move it closer to an emitter and to the depth the deficit models, push it in until the whole sensing length is in firm contact with the soil, then reset the calibration of {probe}: the samples collected so far describe the old position.

placement_poor_contact.title: {probe} jumps while the soil stands still
placement_poor_contact.description:
Between consecutive readings taken while the deficit barely moved, the index of {moisture_entity} changes by {still_raw_step} points.

Soil water does not change that fast. An air gap around the shaft does, and so does a loose connection or a failing probe: the reading follows the air in the cavity rather than the water in the soil.

Pull the probe and reinsert it so the whole sensing length is in firm contact, backfilling and pressing the soil around it rather than dropping it into a wide hole. If the jumps survive a clean reinsertion, suspect the probe itself.

placement_unstable_between_cycles.title: {probe} does not read the same soil twice
placement_unstable_between_cycles.description:
Each cycle on its own looks clean, but the relation between index and water changes from one cycle to the next: across {cycles_considered} cycles the spread is {slope_spread} times the typical value.

The probe is reading correctly, and it is reading a spot that is not representative. Usually the water reaches it differently each time: an emitter that clogs and clears, a probe on the edge of the wetted bulb where a small change in flow moves the boundary past it, or runoff that takes a different path on different days.

Check the emitter that waters {probe} and move the probe well inside the wetted area rather than at its edge. The calibration is not so much wrong as averaging several different situations.

placement_wet_anchor_drift.title: Field capacity keeps reading differently on {probe}
placement_wet_anchor_drift.description:
After each irrigation and drainage the soil is at field capacity by definition, so {moisture_entity} should report about the same index every time. Instead it has moved {wet_anchor_drift} points in one direction across {cycles_considered} cycles.

What is changing is the probe and the soil around it, not the water. The usual causes are the soil settling and pulling away from the shaft, roots growing into the sensing volume, or corroding electrodes.

Pull the probe, check the shaft and the soil contact, reinsert it firmly and reset the calibration of {probe}: the samples collected before the change describe a different instrument.

placement_coarse_response.title: {probe} resolves the soil too coarsely to calibrate well
placement_coarse_response.description:
Across the whole reservoir the index of {moisture_entity} covers about {points_per_reservoir} points, where {points_per_reservoir_required} is the minimum this method expects.

At that resolution one index point is worth more than a percentage point of soil water on its own, so the quantisation of the probe consumes most of the error budget before the calibration adds any of its own. A calibration will still be published if it passes its gates, and it will be blunt.

A deeper or firmer insertion usually widens the range. If it does not, the probe is what it is, and its calibrated value should be read as a coarse indicator rather than a measurement.

placement_outside_wetted_bulb.title: {probe} fills up when it rains and not when the zone is watered
placement_outside_wetted_bulb.description:
Across {rain_cycles} cycles opened by rain and {irrigation_cycles} opened by the irrigation, field capacity read {wet_anchor_gap} index points higher after rain than after watering. Both numbers describe the same soil state: a cycle only opens once the water balance says the profile is nearly full, so what differs is the probe's answer, not the water.

Rain falls on every square centimetre. A dripper wets a bulb around itself, and a probe outside that bulb is watered only by the weather. This is the one failure a single probe cannot diagnose on its own, and the rain gauge is what makes it visible.

Move {probe} to about half the wetted radius from an emitter: 8 to 12 cm on sand, 12 to 20 cm on loam, 20 to 30 cm on clay. Never directly under the emitter. Then reset its calibration: the samples collected so far describe the old position.
